facts.claim: AgriFutures Australia, project 'Farm-based methods for control of flowering in Waratahs' (The University of Sydney, closed): waratah flowering is concentrated in spring; expected outcomes include 'reduction of oversupply in Spring and ability to capitalise on early and late season prices'. The project aimed to extend flowering 'to meet peak demand periods, such as Christmas and Valentine's Day'.

facts.claim: South Australian Metropolitan Fire Service, 'Home fire safety fact sheet: Candles': 'A candle is an open flame. It can easily ignite any combustible items nearby.' and 'Extinguish all candles when leaving a room or going to sleep.' and 'Keep the immediate area around a candle clear of all items. They should be kept well away from items that can catch fire, such as clothing, books, paper, curtains, Christmas trees and flammable decorations etc.'
facts.conflicts: Fact sheet is written for homes, not venues. Use as general candle-safety guidance; venue open-flame rules are separate (booking checklist).

facts.claim: SA MFS candles fact sheet: 'Make sure candles are placed in sturdy holders that will not tip over and place on a secure piece of heat-resistant furniture. Candle holders must be made of material that cannot burn.' and 'Any air movement (draughts) past a candle can cause the candle wax to melt unevenly. The candle may then become unstable and fall over.'
SA MFS candles fact sheet: 'Battery operated candles are a good and safe alternative to traditional candles.'

insider_details.detail: Waratah is the one flower this post can tie to a season: its flowering is concentrated in spring (AgriFutures project page). Name no other flower as in season; link to the flowers hub for seasonality.

Candlelit centrepieces need clear space: a fire service fact sheet says to keep candles well away from items that can catch fire, including flammable decorations, so keep dried grasses, paper menus and trailing greenery clear of the flame.
Use heavy, non-combustible holders on a stable surface, and think about breezes on terraces and in marquees: the same fact sheet warns that draughts make wax melt unevenly and candles can fall over.

Where a venue restricts open flame, battery-operated candles keep the glow; the SA MFS calls them 'a good and safe alternative to traditional candles'. Always ask your venue about open flame before designing around real candles.
Advice, not fact: confirm with your venue whether naked flames, sparklers or hurricane lamps are permitted, and who extinguishes candles at the end of the night.
